label: caiso 25 corridor-deliverability
definition: NEW KEEPER. Adds the measured WECC corridor deliverability limit (--caiso-corridor-flow-limit) on top of the per-hub signed legs: each import corridor's import-direction link flow is capped at the per-(month x hour-of-day) p95 measured net import (an ATC proxy from EIA-930 BA-to-BA interchange; one-sided, export keeps the physical TTC). Fixes the diurnal phase residual -- net-import corr flips POSITIVE both scored years (2024 -0.15->+0.08, 2025 -0.36->+0.03), the first per-hub run with the right diurnal sign -- and fixes 2025 over-import (net -41.1->-36.3 TWh vs actual -36.2). Removing the phantom midday thermal import lifts the body to its honest level (mean 2024 +2.6/2025 +4.9) and drops neg-hours (459->346/193->61): the exposed in-state midday over-pricing residual (next phase), NOT a reason to revert (rule #1). 2024 net now under-imports (-28.3) -- the exposed evening import shortfall. P0->P1, commitment off; 2023 = static-ladder hub fallback but corridor cap active (corr +0.97).
